gm.narrative:
Brenna Holt's broad smile widens as she wipes her hands on her apron and leans across the bar. "Two copper for a good mug of ale, fresh from the cask," she says warmly, already reaching for a tankard. "You look like you've come a ways—first one's on the house if you lend a hand with the evening rush later. The miners are restless about that missing salt cart again, and Osric Vane up in the square is offering decent coin to anyone with steel willing to clear the orc nest off the cut. What do you say?"

The hearth crackles behind you, filling the air with the scent of woodsmoke as a few miners glance your way, their bowls nearly empty.

gm.narrative:
Brenna's eyes light up at your question, and she rests her elbows on the scarred counter, voice dropping to the easy cadence of someone sharing the local pulse. "Work? Plenty, if you've a mind for it. Osric Vane up at the Guild house in the square pays good silver for anyone with steel who'll help clear the orc camp off the cut—raiders have been lifting salt carts again, though the prints never quite match. Or there's my own tables tonight; I'm short a pair of hands with the miners coming in thirsty. Lend one for an hour or two and the stew's on me, plus every scrap of gossip that crosses the bar."

She straightens, glancing toward the door as two more dusty figures shoulder in from the road. "Or if it's honest metal you're after, take your blade down to Hilde Brask's forge off the square—she'll put an edge on it for two copper and might have bellows work if you look strong enough." Her smile returns, warm and expectant, waiting to see which thread you tug first.

gm.narrative:
You step out of the Valley Inn into the cool evening air, boots crunching on the gravel path that curves past the inn yard and up toward the square. The last of the daylight clings to the hills, painting the mud and ore-carts in long shadows while a light breeze carries the metallic tang of tin from the nearby workings. Lanterns already flicker at the guild post, and a few late vendors are packing their stalls as the square empties for the night.

Osric Vane stands near the guild board, ink-stained fingers tapping a rolled parchment against his thigh. His grey coat looks rumpled from a long day, and he glances up at your approach with a faint crease between his brows. "The cut's still crawling with them," he says without preamble, voice clipped. "If you're the one Brenna mentioned, the guild will pay twenty silver to any who clear the nest by week's end. Spears and a map of the approach if you sign on now." He holds your gaze, waiting, the parchment half-unrolled in his hand.
gm.context_summary: In Market Square at evening with Osric Vane; he offers 20 silver to clear the orc nest on the cut, providing spears and a map if accepted; village tension over recent thefts and attacks lingers.

gm.narrative:
Osric Vane's mouth tightens at your agreement, his ink-stained fingers drumming once on the guild post before he catches himself. "Good. Saves me another hour shouting at cowards." He jerks his chin toward a weathered map case leaning against the board and a bundle of sturdy iron-tipped spears propped beside it. "Take what you need. The nest's a half-hour scramble up the cut—three or four of the brutes, by the tracks. Clear them out and the village might breathe again. Twenty silver when you bring proof back."

He glances at the lengthening shadows across the square, voice dropping. "Mind the west road on your way. Folk are saying the Tinjacks are moving again after last night's weighing-shed mess. If you spot anything odd, the Guild hears of it first."

The evening air cools quickly now, carrying the distant clank of ore-carts and the low mutter of miners closing their stalls. Osric waits, arms crossed, for you to claim the gear or ask anything further.

gm.narrative:
You follow the short lane from the square, the evening air cooling as the last of the sun slips behind the hills. The rhythmic clang of hammer on metal grows louder, drawing you to the open-fronted forge where heat rolls out in waves. Hilde Brask glances up from the anvil, her scarred forearms flexing as she quenches a glowing spearhead in the trough; steam hisses up between you. She sets the tool aside and wipes her brow with the back of a thick glove, eyeing you with the wary look of someone who has seen too many strangers asking questions lately.

The half-sorted tin ingots in the nearby crate catch the firelight, their edges still raw. Hilde straightens, her voice blunt but not unfriendly. "Forge is open if you've coin or work. What brings you through my door at this hour?" She nods toward the back lane, where shadows already pool. The village tension lingers here too, thick as the coal smoke.

gm.narrative:
Hilde glances up from the anvil as you speak, hammer paused mid-swing, the heat rippling the air between you. "Something to eat?" she echoes, voice low and edged with the day's weariness. "This isn't the inn, stranger. Brenna's got stew across the square if you're that hungry." She sets the hammer down with a dull clink and wipes soot from her scarred forearm with the edge of her apron, eyes narrowing slightly at the request. "If you're after honest work instead, I could use a hand on the bellows tonight. Pays two silver or a free edge on that knife of yours. Otherwise, best move on before the Tinjacks stir more trouble."

The forge fire crackles louder in the quiet that follows, tin ingots glinting dully in their crate. She waits, one hand resting near the rack of blades, her stance still guarded but not outright dismissive.
